name: Prose Force and Rhythm Rubric
description: Evaluation criteria for a line-editing run using Hart's Wordcraft pass order with the claim-strength invariant, protected-hedge list, escalation discipline, and diagnostics-not-objectives rule. Minimum acceptable standard is an average score of 3.5.

criteria.name: Pass Order and Separation
criteria.description: Whether the ten passes ran in the mandated order, each as its own step with its own output, with Mechanics last and never before Voice

scores.1: All passes collapsed into one 'improve this writing' edit; order not observable in the output
scores.2: Some passes named but edits from different classes appear in the same step; Mechanics ran early
scores.3: Passes run in order but two or three are merged; Mechanics is last
scores.4: All ten passes run separately in the correct order with per-pass output; Mechanics after Voice
scores.5: All ten run separately and in order, each output states which edit class it made and which it declined as out of class

criteria.name: Claim-Strength Invariant
criteria.description: Whether epistemic strength was recorded before rewriting and preserved after, in both directions

scores.1: No ledger; verbs strengthened freely ('associated with' became 'drove', 'suggests' became 'shows')
scores.2: Ledger exists in name but strength changes went unnoticed; at least one claim silently promoted
scores.3: Ledger built for most claim-bearing sentences; strength preserved but silent moves (dropped attribution, scope, date) not tracked
scores.4: Ledger complete with before/after S-levels; all raises reverted and reported; silent moves tracked
scores.5: Complete ledger, reverts reported with rationale, silent strength moves tracked including rounding, and anti-overcorrection checked so sourced facts were not needlessly hedged

criteria.name: Hedge Protection
criteria.description: Whether List A was cut, List B protected, and the scope exception applied instead of blunt deletion

scores.1: Parasite list applied uniformly; 'approximately', 'in this sample', 'as of [date]' deleted from analytical claims
scores.2: List B mostly survived by luck; at least one load-bearing qualifier lost
scores.3: List A cut, List B protected, but scope-carrying List A words deleted outright, converting base rates into universals
scores.4: Both lists applied correctly and the scope exception used where the material supplied the scope
scores.5: Both lists applied, scope exception used, and cases where the material did not supply the scope kept the word and produced a reporting gap entry

criteria.name: Escalation Discipline
criteria.description: Whether defects outside a pass's class were escalated upward rather than compensated for with prose polish

scores.1: No escalations; structural and reporting failures smoothed over with wording changes
scores.2: Escalation mentioned as a concept but every defect was fixed in place
scores.3: Some escalations filed but without the class, reason, or target layer
scores.4: Escalation records complete (defect, real class, why not fixable here, target layer) and passed downstream
scores.5: Complete escalation records plus a reporting-gap register, with a passive construction correctly left intact where the actor was unnamed rather than an actor invented

criteria.name: Metrics as Diagnostics
criteria.description: Whether rhythm and brevity numbers were reported alongside the prose rather than optimized into it

scores.1: Variance maximized with fragments and one-word sentences; targets hit, register wrecked
scores.2: Metrics driven directly; sentences chopped or padded to reach numbers
scores.3: Metrics reported and used to guide edits, but no record of what was declined
scores.4: Metrics reported with the reading and the action taken; fixes made at clause level, not by fragments
scores.5: Metrics reported with reading, action, and an explicit 'declined' line; clarity split log respected so rhythm did not undo clarity

criteria.name: Provenance and Attribution Honesty
criteria.description: Whether numeric thresholds were labelled as derived defaults and attributions were made correctly

scores.1: Thresholds presented as 'Hart says'; 'the Oregon Method' or the SCAM acronym cited as Hart's
scores.3: Thresholds labelled as defaults somewhere; attributions correct but unstated
scores.4: Thresholds labelled as derived operational defaults in the config and the report; attributions correct
scores.5: Thresholds shipped as tunable config with the full provenance note, and attribution caveats carried explicitly where relevant

criteria.name: System-Protagonist Handling
criteria.description: Whether force and humanity passes avoided personifying markets, protocols, institutions, and pipelines

scores.1: Systems decide, want, believe, and fear throughout; intent asserted across every verb
scores.2: Personification used repeatedly with no sweep run
scores.3: Anthropomorphism sweep run but some intention verbs survive on non-human subjects
scores.4: Sweep run and clean; systems given state-change verbs, named operators, or named constraints
scores.5: Sweep clean, re-run after the humanity pass, and any single deliberate personification is declared as a framing device rather than distributed through the piece

criteria.name: Slop Audit Execution
criteria.description: Whether the final audit ran in its internal order, respected the hedge carve-out, and avoided the anti-slop tic

scores.1: Audit skipped, or hedge removal stripped genuine evidential uncertainty
scores.2: Audit run out of order; specificity sweep invented specifics it lacked
scores.3: Audit run in order; hedge carve-out respected but no meaning re-check at step 13
scores.4: Full 13 steps in order, carve-out respected, step 13 re-check performed, Mechanics re-run on changed lines
scores.5: All of the above, plus no overcorrection into a second uniformity (no categorical em-dash ban, no sprinkled fragments, no performed casualness), and unfillable specificity gaps stated openly
